own_solution.law: Steady conduction through series thermal resistances gives P = deltaT/(Ra + Rb). The base flow is 20/0.25 = 80 W. Warming the hotter wall surface by x gives P = (20 + x)/0.25. Specifying the colder surface temperature cancels through deltaT = (Tc + 20) - Tc.
assumptions: The specified thermal resistances remain applicable at all listed temperatures.
The final heat flow is steady, with no edge losses.
The adjacent partition has no specified thermal connection to the wall.
The earlier test does not change the stated initial conditions of the present test.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T6D07 and T97D1 replace their twins' explicit 6.5 K with 'a few kelvin', violating the review instructions' requirement that variants of the same quantity preserve its stated numerical value and unit.

notes: All physical classifications, certified numerical answers, resistance relations and units check out: wall warming by 3.5, 6.5 and 11 K gives 94, 106 and 124 W; both absolute-temperature variants give 80 W at every listed temperature; both disconnected attachments leave 80 W. The explicitly declared minimal_pair_with pairs preserve their numerical values and units, and the earlier-test attachment is the intended event change. This corrects my pass-1 suggestion that the temporal attachment change itself was an additional defect. The authors explain that the numeral-free twins are deliberate controls, rather than claiming they preserve 6.5 K. Nevertheless, the frozen review instructions supply no exemption for such controls from the numerical-matching requirement, so the rendering defect and invalid verdict remain.
